title: Affine etale realization commutes with derived Hom from a bounded-above coherent source
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Use the exact associated etale module functor $a_A$ of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $E,F\in D(A)$. Assume every $H^i(E)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $H^i(E)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$, and $H^i(F)=0$ for all sufficiently negative $i$. For the explicit size presentation take $A$ and ordinary $A$-modules in universe $u$; the small etale site's object and arrow universes are $u+1$ and $u$. Let $i$ be the canonical sectionwise universe transport sending a module sheaf $M$ to $\operatorname{ULift}M$ with its original structure-ring action and restriction maps conjugated by $\operatorname{ULift.up/down}$; the section identification is $\operatorname{ULift.down}$ with inverse $\operatorname{ULift.up}$. Put $a'_A=i\circ a_A$, also denoting its exact termwise derived realization by $a'_A$. There is a natural isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category of $\mathcal O_U$-module sheaves on the same small etale site, with section universe $u+1$:
$$a'_A\bigl(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,F)\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}\bigl(a'_A(E),a'_A(F)\bigr).$$
The two derived Homs are [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], in its ordinary-module presentation over $A$ and its ringed-site presentation on the small etale site of $U$, respectively. The latter keeps the actual structure rings in universe $u$. Naturality is contravariant in $E$ and covariant in $F$ on the full category of pairs satisfying the stated hypotheses. No finite-generation hypothesis on the cohomology of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08JP (lemma-descend-RHom), case (1), combined with perfect.tex lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian and lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom (affine clause (3)(a)).

proof.text: The Noetherian cohomology criterion makes $E$ pseudo-coherent over $A$: the required upper bound and finite generation are exactly our hypotheses. By the definition, choose a bounded-above finite free complex $P^\bullet$ representing $E$.

Put $\widetilde E,\widetilde F$ for the Zariski affine derived realizations. The affine equivalence sends $P^\bullet$ to its termwise tilde complex; finite free terms become finite free structure modules, so $\widetilde E$ is pseudo-coherent by definition. The tilde homology comparison gives $H^i(\widetilde F)\cong\widetilde{H^i(F)}$, so the given lower bound for $F$ also bounds $\widetilde F$.

Let $b$ bound $P^\bullet$ above and represent $F$ by a complex $F^\bullet$ with $F^q=0$ for $q<a$, where $H^i(F)=0$ for $i<a$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. By [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom], $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(P^\bullet,F^\bullet)$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,F)$. The termwise tilde $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ represents $\widetilde E$ and has finite free terms [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module]; so [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model], applied to its identity and to $\widetilde{F^\bullet}$, shows that $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\widetilde{P^\bullet},\widetilde{F^\bullet})$ represents $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\widetilde E,\widetilde F)$. In degree $n$ only the finitely many $p$ with $a-n\le p\le b$ contribute to either product. For $P^p\cong A^m$ both $\widetilde{\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^p,F^q)}$ and $\mathcal Hom(\widetilde{P^p},\widetilde{F^q})$ are $(\widetilde{F^q})^m$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], identified by $h\mapsto\widetilde h$; this commutes with $d_Fh-(-1)^nhd_P$ because tilde is an additive functor. The resulting isomorphism of complexes gives $\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,F)}\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\widetilde E,\widetilde F)$, with an explicit map rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, clause (3)(a) and its proof (finite projective Hom-complex computation, cohomology.tex lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free).

proof.text: For every $A$-module $M$, the restriction of $a_A(M)$ to affine Zariski opens $D(f)$ has sections $A_f\otimes_A M=M_f$, with the localization restrictions. These are exactly the sections of $\widetilde M$. Both sheaves are quasi-coherent; the Zariski/etale equivalence, whose inverse is restriction, therefore gives the natural identification $\epsilon_U^*\widetilde M\cong a_A(M)$. Apply it termwise to complexes and localize: both functors are exact, hence it identifies $\epsilon_U^*\widetilde T$ with $a_A(T)$ for every $T\in D(A)$.

Apply $\epsilon_U^*$ to the isomorphism of step 3 and compose with the comparison of [lem-sfb-zariski-etale-pseudocoherent-rhom] for $K=\widetilde E$, $L=\widetilde F$, whose hypotheses were checked in step 2. The identifications of step 4, for $T=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(E,F)$, $E$ and $F$, turn the composite into the required isomorphism. Naturality: a morphism $E\to E'$ in $D(A)$ is represented by a chain map $P^\bullet\to P'^\bullet$ of the finite free models, as bounded-above projective complexes are K-projective [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective]; a morphism $F\to F'$ is represented by a chain map from $F^\bullet$ into a bounded-below injective, K-injective resolution of $F'^\bullet$ [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], to which step 3 applies equally. Precomposition and postcomposition commute with $h\mapsto\widetilde h$, so the step-3 isomorphism is natural; the new comparison is natural by its statement and step 4 is natural in $T$. No finiteness condition on $F$ has been used.
